added_fields.copybot_families: VOCABULARY.json tag ids only (subset of copybot_links semantics)
added_fields.post_2022_data: true if the sample includes data after 2022-01-01 (as stated by the source)
added_fields.net_of_cost_evidence: no / partial / yes(...) - whether the source itself compares the effect with trading costs

order: director order 51 P2 support (literature register extension)
rules: only sources opened in this session (url_opened); numbers copied from opened abstract/PDF text or UNKNOWN; summaries in own words; no market data fetched; existing E01-E44 untouched

entries.title: Crypto Carry
entries.authors: Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf; Karamfil Todorov
entries.venue: CEPR Discussion Paper 20719 (Oct 2025); later version of BIS WP 1087 (E04)
entries.mechanism: futures-spot carry as a volatile 'inconvenience yield' of spot: trend-chasing leveraged demand meets scarce arbitrage capital (regulatory and margin frictions)
entries.effect_size: carry sometimes above 40% p.a.; strongly time-varying (abstract)
entries.gross_or_net: gross (carry level, not a trading P&L)
entries.capacity_notes: authors attribute persistence to limited arbitrage capital; not quantified
entries.oos_or_replication: updated version of E04; the headline level wording moved from 'up to 60%' (E04) to 'sometimes exceeding 40%'
entries.notes: Management Science version (doi 10.1287/mnsc.2024.05069) still 403 in this session; the CEPR 2025 abstract is the newest verified text. Level only, no net result.

entries.title: Designing funding rates for perpetual futures in cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Jaehyun Kim; Hyungbin Park
entries.mechanism: funding-rate design that keeps perp price at a target value; replicating portfolios; path-dependent funding (BSDE theory)
entries.effect_size: n/a (theory)
entries.notes: Theory only. Useful for understanding why funding formulas (premium index + clamp) mechanically anchor the perp; no empirical predictability claim.

entries.title: A primer on perpetuals
entries.authors: Guillermo Angeris; Tarun Chitra; Alex Evans; Matthew Lorig
entries.mechanism: model-free funding and discount rates for perpetual contracts; replication of the short side; jump case semi-robust
entries.effect_size: n/a (theory)
entries.notes: Theory; frictionless, no transaction costs by assumption.

entries.title: Where Are the Rates? Derivative-Implied Interest Rates in Cryptocurrency Markets
entries.authors: Philippe Bergault; Sébastien Bieber; Olivier Guéant; Wenkai Zhang
entries.mechanism: USD and coin discount factors jointly inferred from inverse options (put-call parity) and futures basis
entries.market: Deribit BTC and ETH options and futures (hourly)
entries.effect_size: implied USD rates average about 8% per year and rose in the 2024 rallies; implied BTC/ETH rates near zero; persistent gap vs Aave USDC rates
entries.notes: Post-2022 evidence that the derivative-implied USD rate (the carry benchmark) is about 8% p.a. and disconnected from DeFi lending rates (limited integration). Deribit data is outside host gates; the concept transfers to Binance dated USD-M basis (F2), which is AVAILABLE_FORWARD.

entries.title: Arbitrage, contract design, and market structure in Bitcoin futures markets
entries.authors: Riccardo De Blasis; Alexander Webb
entries.mechanism: quarterly vs perpetual contract design; intraday patterns in perps; cash-and-carry opportunities
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: perps show multiple u-shaped intraday curves, seasonal and opening effects; quarterly cash-and-carry opportunities mainly during market dislocations)
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed support for 'basis opportunities cluster in dislocations' (cf. E04 margin spikes). Intraday perp seasonality relevant to K3 funding-time question.

entries.title: Bitcoin futures risk premia
entries.authors: Shimeng Shi
entries.mechanism: position-based (trader-category positioning), microstructure and macro predictors of bitcoin futures returns
entries.market: regulated bitcoin futures (positions by trader type; venue not stated in abstract)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: trading activity and extreme speculator/retail sentiment predict futures price changes; lower transaction cost goes with higher premia; speculators negative-feedback, retail positive-feedback)
entries.notes: Positioning data by trader category is a regulated-futures (COT-type) concept; not in lab gates. Retail positive-feedback finding is consistent with the trend-chasing demand story of E04 and X001.

entries.title: Jump risk premia in the presence of clustered jumps
entries.authors: Francis Liu; Natalie Packham; Artur Sepp
entries.mechanism: bivariate Hawkes jumps; positive/negative jump premia inferred from BTC options; skew can change sign with sentiment
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: inferred jump premia have predictive power for BTC futures cost of carry and for delta-hedged option P&L)
entries.notes: Links option-implied jump premia to futures carry; options data outside gates.

entries.title: Dynamic Collateral Control for Permissionless Spot Perpetual Basis Trading
entries.authors: Anatoly Krestenko; Mikhail Butov; Rostislav Berezovskiy; Danila Bolotin
entries.mechanism: spot long + short perp basis trade as a collateral-allocation control problem under on-chain execution frictions
entries.market: DeFi spot and perpetuals (BTC, LINK, DOGE among calibrated assets)
entries.universe: BTC, LINK, DOGE and others (UNKNOWN full list)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: required collateral lowest for BTC and much higher for long-tail assets; realised execution wedges significant, worse when selling the basis; realised performance mostly explained by the funding environment)
entries.gross_or_net: net of modelled execution wedges (live routed execution measured)
entries.capacity_notes: collateral need rises with volatility stress and for long-tail assets
entries.oos_or_replication: historical backtest + live routed execution test
entries.notes: No headline return number in abstract. Key qualitative point for the lab: basis P&L is driven by the funding regime, and execution wedges are material. CEX analogue AVAILABLE_FORWARD; DeFi venues not collected.

entries.title: Liquidation, Leverage and Optimal Margin in Bitcoin Futures Markets
entries.authors: Zhiyong Cheng; Jun Deng; Tianyi Wang; Mei Yu
entries.mechanism: extreme-value tails of perp returns vs forced liquidations and margin levels
entries.effect_size: daily forced liquidations average 3.51% (long) and 1.89% (short) of outstanding futures; liquidated traders use about 60x leverage on average; margin of 33% (long) / 20% (short) needed for 1% daily margin-call probability
entries.notes: Scale of forced flow on a pre-2021 venue. Per-order liquidation data in the lab collector is UNKNOWN (same as E16). Not a price-response study.

entries.title: Towards Understanding Cryptocurrency Derivatives: A Case Study of BitMEX
entries.authors: Kyle Soska; Jin-Dong Dong; Alex Khodaverdian; Ariel Zetlin-Jones; Bryan Routledge; Nicolas Christin
entries.mechanism: leverage and public liquidation events vs discrete price jumps ('barts')
entries.effect_size: over 425,000 liquidation events collected; weekly liquidations peaked near USD 1bn (Nov 2018); liquidation events above USD 100M every few weeks in 2018 coincided with discrete jumps; long liquidations dominate even in up-trends; 1 Apr 2019 25% spot jump liquidated over USD 400M of shorts
entries.effect_unit_horizon: USD liquidated per day/week (7-day moving average)
entries.oos_or_replication: descriptive; authors state causality between leverage and jumps is unresolved
entries.notes: Same CMU group as E05. Important caveat stated by the authors: correlation of liquidations with jumps, not shown causal; no post-liquidation return statistics.

entries.title: Hedging with Bitcoin Futures: The Effect of Liquidation Loss Aversion and Aggressive Trading
entries.authors: Carol Alexander; Jun Deng; Bin Zou
entries.mechanism: optimal hedge under automatic liquidation risk; liquidation probability by leverage and horizon
entries.market: 7 BTC direct and inverse hedging instruments on 5 exchanges (BitMEX, Binance, Bybit, Deribit, OKEx), minute data
entries.period: sample ends May 2021; includes 11-14 Mar 2020 and 18-21 May 2021 crashes
entries.effect_size: 19 May 2021: USD 8.6bn liquidations reported across products and exchanges; Binance liquidation reports for May judged inaccurate; 100x positions: over 95% of 1-day positions end in liquidation; 30-day horizon: 5x shorts above 60% liquidation probability
entries.effect_unit_horizon: liquidation probability per holding horizon; USD liquidated per day
entries.notes: Data-quality warning: exchange-reported liquidation feeds can be wrong (Binance, May 2021) - relevant if the lab ever uses liquidation feeds. Leverage/liquidation tables relevant to carry margin realism.

entries.title: Where does the criticality live? Early-warning signals are event-heterogeneous across seven crypto-perpetual liquidation cascades
entries.authors: Ramon Marc Garcia Seuma
entries.mechanism: critical-slowing-down early-warning signals (variance, lag-1 autocorrelation) before liquidation cascades
entries.market: Binance BTC perpetual (minute price, 5-minute leverage and taker flow)
entries.effect_size: no variable warns in all events; price shows the signature in 5 of 7 events, absent in the 2 tariff-news shocks; only taker order-flow variance compression survives all events (300-onset placebo, Fisher p about 5e-6) and only as a population-level precursor
entries.oos_or_replication: out-of-event check: the Oct 2025 in-sample signature did not generalise
entries.notes: Single author, very recent, not replicated. Strong negative result: no per-event alarm. Minute prices and taker flow are collectable forward; 5-min OI/positioning availability: UNKNOWN.

entries.title: Measuring the engine of a liquidation cascade: subcritical branching inside a first-order transition
entries.authors: Ramon Marc Garcia Seuma
entries.mechanism: branching ratio of forced selling; liquidity withdrawal vs multiplier as the driver of cascade severity
entries.market: seven crypto-perp cascades; fill-level data from one fully transparent on-chain venue for Oct 2025
entries.effect_size: Oct 2025 branching ratio about 0.1-0.2 (subcritical); 88% of post-onset forced selling within 30 minutes; 63% absorbed off-book by the venue backstop; open interest cleared by 25-70%; inter-asset coupling jumps 1.6-4.4 baseline SD at onset
entries.oos_or_replication: subsampling invariance reported; Galton-Watson pre-state model rejected at simulated power >= 0.96
entries.notes: Venue not named in abstract (described as fully transparent with a backstop). Consistent with E16 that the cascade signature is in liquidity. Still no post-cascade return reversal statistic.

entries.title: Autodeleveraging: Impossibilities and Optimization
entries.authors: Tarun Chitra
entries.mechanism: auto-deleveraging (ADL) as loss socialisation when liquidations fail; solvency/revenue/fairness trilemma
entries.market: Hyperliquid perps (10 Oct 2025); comparison with Binance
entries.effect_size: ADL closed USD 2.1bn of positions in 12 minutes; production ADL overshot the needed haircut: excess profit taken from winners USD 45.0-51.7M (about USD 653.6M of positions); Binance judged to over-use ADL more than Hyperliquid
entries.notes: Direct relevance to hedged books: a profitable short-perp hedge leg can be force-closed by ADL in a crash (tail risk for carry not priced in E05/E08).

entries.title: Reconciling Open Interest with Traded Volume in Perpetual Swaps
entries.authors: Ioannis Giagkiozis; Emilio Said
entries.mechanism: consistency check of reported open interest against tick-level traded volume
entries.market: BTC perpetual swaps on 7 of the most liquid derivatives exchanges
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN magnitude (abstract: OI systematically misquoted by some large exchanges; some implausible, some apparently delaying liquidation messages)
entries.notes: Data-quality source: OI and liquidation feeds may be unreliable per venue. Supports X038's finding that OI publication time is unverifiable on public archives.

entries.title: Systemic fragility in decentralised markets
entries.authors: Alfred Lehar; Christine A Parlour
entries.mechanism: flash-loan liquidators must sell seized collateral immediately; price impact spreads from DEXs to other venues
entries.market: Compound and Aave liquidations; price impact on 9 DEXs
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: temporary and permanent price impact like equity block trades; effect on return distributions documented)
entries.notes: Forced liquidation sales have a permanent component -> argues against assuming full reversal. On-chain data not available in the lab.

entries.title: Liquidation Mechanisms and Price Impacts in DeFi
entries.authors: Phoebe Tian; Yu Zhu
entries.venue: Bank of Canada Staff Working Paper 2025-12
entries.mechanism: fixed-spread vs auction liquidations; participation cost sets liquidator competition and price impact
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: auction-based liquidations give smaller price drops when participation cost is low)
entries.notes: Mechanism design shapes the size of liquidation price impact; no return-reversal statistic.

entries.title: An Empirical Study of DeFi Liquidations: Incentives, Risks, and Instabilities
entries.authors: Kaihua Qin; Liyi Zhou; Pablo Gamito; Philipp Jovanovic; Arthur Gervais
entries.mechanism: liquidation designs of Aave, Compound, MakerDAO, dYdX; liquidator incentives and borrower losses
entries.market: Ethereum DeFi lending (over 85% of lending market)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN headline size (abstract: designs over-sell discounted collateral at borrowers' expense; TVL context USD 39.88bn)
entries.notes: DeFi liquidation microstructure; not CEX perps.

entries.title: Liquidations: DeFi on a Knife-edge
entries.authors: Daniel Perez; Sam M. Werner; Jiahua Xu; Benjamin Livshits
entries.venue: Financial Cryptography and Data Security 2021 (LNCS); arXiv:2009.13235
entries.mechanism: sensitivity of liquidable debt to small price moves; liquidator efficiency
entries.effect_size: a 3% price move can make over USD 10M liquidable; over 70% of liquidable positions are liquidated immediately
entries.effect_unit_horizon: USD liquidable per % price move; share liquidated immediately
entries.notes: Shows liquidation thresholds cluster -> cascade fuel; pre-2021 DeFi only.

entries.title: Cryptocurrency return reversals
entries.authors: Steven E. Kozlowski; Michael R. Puleo; Jizhou Zhou
entries.mechanism: cross-sectional short-term reversal as market inefficiency plus liquidity-provision compensation
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: significant reversal at daily, weekly and monthly rebalancing; both sample halves; strongest in small, illiquid coins)
entries.notes: Monthly reversal here differs from E15/E14 large-coin momentum; same small/illiquid concentration.

entries.title: Trading volume and liquidity provision in cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Daniele Bianchi; Mykola Babiak; Alexander Dickerson
entries.mechanism: short-term reversal as return to liquidity provision; lagged return x volume interaction (inventory risk, adverse selection)
entries.market: USD crypto pairs on multiple centralised exchanges
entries.universe: moderately large cross-section of USD pairs
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: reversal returns concentrated in low-activity pairs, larger in small, volatile, illiquid pairs)
entries.notes: Peer-reviewed confirmation that reversal sits where the lab does not trade (low-activity pairs).

entries.title: Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement
entries.authors: Nadav A. Kitron; Jonathan M. Wengrowicz
entries.mechanism: 15-minute directional mean reversion; conditioning on aggressive taker flow (compensated liquidity provision)
entries.market: Binance spot pairs vs US stocks/ETFs
entries.effect_size: significant directional reversal in 90% of 183 Binance pairs vs 2.7% of US names; gross edge peaks near 1.3 bp per trade vs 5 bp round-trip cost; AUC gap +0.011 (95% CI +0.008 to +0.014) under the most conservative accounting
entries.gross_or_net: gross edge compared explicitly against cost
entries.costs_included: compared: 5 bp round trip exceeds the 1.3 bp gross edge
entries.capacity_notes: edge below cost -> not capturable at benchmark spot costs
entries.oos_or_replication: strictly out-of-sample protocol, permutation null, frozen 6-month holdout
entries.notes: Post-2022, liquid venue, explicit cost comparison: statistically real, economically below taker cost. Matches the lab's SCREEN_FAIL on MOVESCREEN.

entries.title: New behaviorally-based cross-sectional reversal portfolios in the cryptocurrency market and market uncertainty
entries.authors: Kei Nakagawa; Ryuta Sakemoto
entries.mechanism: reversal portfolios anchored on the formation-period low (behavioural decomposition)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: higher returns than conventional reversal; robust to conservative transaction costs; hedge vs stock/gold uncertainty)
entries.notes: Claim of cost-robustness without stated size; universe/liquidity screen UNKNOWN -> weak until full text.

entries.title: Explainable Patterns in Cryptocurrency Microstructure
entries.authors: Bartosz Bieganowski; Robert Ślepaczuk
entries.mechanism: order-book/trade features (order flow imbalance, spread, adverse selection) in a CatBoost model; SHAP shapes stable across assets
entries.market: Binance Futures perpetuals, 1-second order books and trades
entries.effect_size: taker backtest annualised return on capital: BTC 0.13 (buy-and-hold 0.83), ENJ 4.06, ETC 5.78, LTC 0.07, ROSE 7.00 (ROSE largely from 10 Oct 2025); maker backtest BTC 2.93, others near zero or negative
entries.effect_unit_horizon: annualised return on capital (fraction) of fixed-notional strategy
entries.gross_or_net: UNKNOWN which table is fee-adjusted (text says gross and taker-fee-adjusted are reported); latency not modelled
entries.costs_included: spread crossing yes (taker at best bid/ask, pessimistic marking); latency no; fees UNKNOWN per table
entries.capacity_notes: authors call results an upper bound in the fastest regime
entries.oos_or_replication: time-series cross-validation; robustness around a flash crash
entries.notes: Trade-level and 1-second book data needed; collector trade-level storage UNKNOWN. BTC taker result is below buy-and-hold; strong results come from small coins and one crash day.

entries.title: The Market Maker's Dilemma: Navigating the Fill Probability vs. Post-Fill Returns Trade-Off
entries.authors: Jakob Albers; Mihai Cucuringu; Sam Howison; Alexander Y. Shestopaloff
entries.mechanism: maker fill probability negatively related to post-fill returns (adverse selection); contrarian quoting vs book imbalance
entries.market: Binance BTC perpetual, live trading experiment
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: negative correlation between fill likelihood and post-fill return; commonly cited maker strategies highly unprofitable)
entries.effect_unit_horizon: post-fill return over immediate to short horizons
entries.notes: Live evidence of adverse selection for passive orders on the lab's main venue; consistent with Bieganowski maker-vs-taker contrast.

entries.title: Order flow analysis of cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Eduard Silantyev
entries.mechanism: Cont-style order flow imbalance and trade flow imbalance vs contemporaneous price change
entries.market: BitMEX XBTUSD perpetual trades and quotes
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN coefficients (abstract: trade flow imbalance explains contemporaneous price changes better than aggregate OFI; strong linear relation over long enough intervals)
entries.notes: Contemporaneous (not predictive) OFI relation; replicates the equity Cont-Kukanov-Stoikov form on a crypto perp. Thin depth and slow updates noted.

entries.title: High-Frequency Jump Analysis of the Bitcoin Market
entries.authors: Olivier Scaillet; Adrien Treccani; Christopher Trevisan
entries.venue: arXiv:1704.08175 (journal version not verified in this session)
entries.mechanism: jumps predicted by order flow imbalance, aggressive traders and spread widening; persistent post-jump price change
entries.market: Mt. Gox tick data with trader identifiers
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: jumps frequent and clustered; OFI, aggressive traders and wider spreads predict them; jumps bring a persistent price change)
entries.notes: Persistent post-jump price change contradicts a naive 'jumps revert' premise; very old single-venue data.

entries.title: A Million Metaorder Analysis of Market Impact on the Bitcoin
entries.authors: Jonathan Donier; Julius Bonart
entries.mechanism: square-root market impact of metaorders; informed vs uninformed flow decomposition
entries.effect_size: square-root impact law holds over four decades of size; uninformed impact decays almost completely
entries.notes: Cost-model input: impact grows with the square root of size, so capacity is concave.

entries.title: Trading in the Sunshine or in the Shade: Market Impact and Adverse Selection on Hyperliquid
entries.authors: Davide Barone; Fabrizio Lillo
entries.mechanism: pre-announced (visible TWAP) vs hidden metaorders: execution cost, permanent impact, liquidity response
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: visible TWAPs pay lower execution cost and leave smaller permanent impact; hidden orders alongside same-side TWAP pay more; displayed depth rises during TWAPs)
entries.notes: Hyperliquid-specific execution evidence. Address-level fills are public on-chain, but the lab does not collect them (UNKNOWN).

entries.title: The intraday dynamics of bitcoin
entries.authors: Andrea Eross; Frank McGroarty; Andrew Urquhart; Simon Wolfe
entries.venue: Research in International Business and Finance 49, 71-81
entries.mechanism: intraday seasonality of volume, volatility and liquidity aligned with global market opening times
entries.market: leading BTC exchange by information share, 5-minute GMT data
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: volume rises through the day and falls from about 16:00 to midnight GMT; volatility highest at opening of major stock markets; liquidity highest at major exchange openings, illiquid early morning)
entries.notes: Pre-2018 spot data.

entries.title: Periodicity in Cryptocurrency Volatility and Liquidity
entries.authors: Peter Reinhard Hansen; Chan Kim; Wade Kimbrough
entries.mechanism: day-of-week, hour-of-day and within-hour patterns in volatility and volume, linked to algorithmic trading and futures funding times
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: systematic patterns at all three periodicities, growing stronger over the years; DEX price adjustment sluggish)
entries.notes: The only verified source linking intraday patterns to funding settlement times (the K3 question) - qualitative only. Same authors as E19 (Kim & Hansen).

entries.title: Bitcoin spot and futures market microstructure
entries.authors: Saketh Aleti; Bruce Mizrach
entries.mechanism: spreads, trade sizes, impact, latency and price discovery across CME and spot exchanges
entries.market: CME BTC futures and 4 USD settlement spot exchanges
entries.effect_size: average bid-ask spread 0.0298%; trades above USD 1M move prices less than 1%; spreads exceed 0.8% for only 226 seconds; most executions trade through better quotes (est. USD 36M losses); CME leads price discovery; BTC leads ETH
entries.notes: Cost benchmark (about 3 bp spread on USD spot). Trade-through losses imply fragmentation cost (cf. X035).

entries.title: What drives the liquidity of cryptocurrencies? A long-term analysis
entries.authors: Alexander Brauneis; Roland Mestel; Erik Theissen
entries.mechanism: determinants of Abdi-Ranaldo spreads: volatility, dollar volume, number of trades
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: volatility, dollar volume and trade count are the main drivers; general financial market variables have no explanatory power)
entries.notes: Companion to E17 (same group).

entries.title: Exchange market share, market makers, and murky behavior: The impact of no-fee trading on cryptocurrency market quality
entries.authors: Luca Galati
entries.mechanism: removal of maker-taker fees (Binance BTC, July 2022) as natural experiment: market makers widen spreads and thin depth
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: spreads wider, depth shallower; total transaction costs for customers rose despite zero fees)
entries.notes: Post-2022 peer-reviewed cost evidence on the lab's venue: headline fee is a poor proxy for total cost; spread/depth must be measured (the lab does).

entries.title: Fragmentation in the Bitcoin market: Evidence from multiple coexisting order books
entries.authors: Yoontae Jeon; Laleh Samarbakhsh; Kenji Hewitt
entries.mechanism: consolidated order book of 5 exchanges; fragmentation cost; smart order routing
entries.market: 5 major BTC exchanges, intraday book snapshots
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: exchange liquidity measure significantly negative even for small trades)

entries.title: The Role of Binance in Bitcoin Volatility Transmission
entries.authors: Carol Alexander; Daniel Heck; Andreas Kaeck
entries.mechanism: realised-volatility spillovers across BTC/USD and BTC/USDT spot and derivatives
entries.market: BTC/USD and BTC/USDT instruments incl. Binance USDT-margined perpetual
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: Binance USDT-margined perp is the main volatility transmitter; interconnectedness higher when Western stock markets are open)
entries.notes: Volatility (not return) leadership of the perp.

entries.title: On The Quality Of Cryptocurrency Markets: Centralized Versus Decentralized Exchanges
entries.authors: Andrea Barbon; Angelo Ranaldo
entries.mechanism: gas fees as fixed costs on DEXs; arbitrage deviations CEX vs DEX
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: gas fees burden small DEX trades and cause persistent arbitrage deviations; DEXs cheaper for large trades)
entries.notes: Explains why visible CEX-DEX gaps persist (fixed costs), consistent with RESULTS_arb_v1 finding 0 opportunities net.

entries.title: Point-in-Time Audit Before Alpha: Public-Archive Availability and a Negative Matched-Budget Study on BTC Perpetual Futures
entries.authors: Baocheng Zeng; Jinhao Yang; Peilin Han; Kangnan He
entries.mechanism: point-in-time availability audit of public Binance archives; matched-budget search vs random search; one-time holdout
entries.market: Binance BTCUSDT USD-M perpetual public archive (trades, mark, index, funding, OI)
entries.effect_size: longest gapless 5-minute intersection of all streams only 304.57 days; auditing cut mean false passes from 0.2910 to 0.0625 on null signals; adaptive agent tied random search; in holdout all runs had positive IC but negative net Sharpe under primary costs
entries.effect_unit_horizon: IC and net Sharpe of factor templates
entries.notes: Methodological twin of the lab's evaluator discipline: positive IC does not survive costs; OI publication time unverifiable on public archives (cf. X015).

entries.title: Cryptocurrency Cross-listing Incentives and Abnormal Returns
entries.authors: Sebastian Laucht
entries.venue: Master thesis, Erasmus School of Economics (final 09-09-2022)
entries.mechanism: cross-listing returns by exchange volume, licensing and reputation (segmentation, liquidity, disclosure theories)
entries.effect_size: listing-day abnormal return 2.35% (constant-mean model); CAAR [-3,+3] about 9.5%; positive before the listing, negative afterwards
entries.notes: Master thesis (not peer reviewed) but extends E20 to 2020-2021: run-up before, decline after -> the post-listing leg is negative.

entries.title: Cross-listings of blockchain-based tokens issued through initial coin offerings: Do liquidity and specific cryptocurrency exchanges matter?
entries.authors: Lennart Ante; André Meyer
entries.mechanism: cross-listing abnormal returns by exchange and pre-listing liquidity
entries.effect_size: abnormal return 6.51% on listing day and 9.97% over a 7-day window; up to 34% on the event day for some exchanges, negligible for others; lower prior volume and market cap -> higher listing return
entries.notes: Same author as E20; overlapping era -> not independent replication.

entries.title: A New Wolf in Town? Pump-and-Dump Manipulation in Cryptocurrency Markets
entries.authors: Anirudh Dhawan; Tālis J. Putniņš
entries.mechanism: openly announced pump-and-dump schemes; overconfidence and gambling preferences explain participation
entries.market: small-cap coins targeted by Telegram pump groups
entries.effect_size: pumps create average price distortions of 65% and abnormal volume in the millions of USD; participants face negative expected returns
entries.notes: Manipulation risk in illiquid listings; relevant as a data-quality filter.

entries.title: Market Efficiency in a Changing Asset Population: Mobility, Entry, and Survival over Cryptocurrency's Full History
entries.authors: Antonis Ballis; Christos Ioannidis
entries.mechanism: Markov mobility across the market-cap distribution; entry/exit observed; neglected-coin premium
entries.effect_size: mobility asymmetry falls about 70% over eras; bottom decile earns 27.5% per week on paper and nothing among assets that trade, with capacity of USD 293,000
entries.gross_or_net: gross on paper vs tradable subset
entries.net_of_cost_evidence: yes (paper premium disappears when tradability imposed)
entries.notes: Search snippet also claimed delisted-as-total-loss cuts a 'frontier premium' by a quarter; not in the opened abstract -> not used.

entries.title: Market reactions to Crypto-Specific announcements: Analyzing behaviors in coins and tokens
entries.authors: Jaeho Myeong; Donghoon Kim
entries.mechanism: price, volatility, volume and wallet-activity response to project disclosures (Xangle platform)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: positive and neutral announcements give significant cumulative-return increases with volatility and volume spikes; wallet transactions fall; negative news mixed)
entries.notes: Xangle is a Korean disclosure platform - closest verified source to the Upbit/Korea announcement channel; no Upbit-listing-specific study was verified.

entries.title: The influence of stablecoin issuances on cryptocurrency markets
entries.authors: Lennart Ante; Ingo Fiedler; Elias Strehle
entries.mechanism: stablecoin issuance events and crypto returns (event study)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: market falls in the week before issuance; positive abnormal returns in the 24 hours around issuance; issuance size not significant; some subsamples insignificant)
entries.notes: Pattern 'issuance after downturn' matches E26; one-year pre-2021 sample.

entries.title: The impact of transparent money flows: Effects of stablecoin transfers on the returns and trading volume of Bitcoin
entries.authors: Lennart Ante; Ingo Fiedler; Elias Strehle
entries.mechanism: large stablecoin transfers by sender/receiver type (unknown, exchange, treasury) vs BTC returns and volume
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: highly significant abnormal volume and significant abnormal returns in the hours around transfers; effects differ across 9 sender-receiver subsamples)
entries.notes: Requires address labelling (vendor).

entries.title: Tethered, or Untethered? On the interplay between stablecoins and major cryptoassets
entries.authors: Ladislav Kristoufek
entries.mechanism: directed spillovers (GVAR forecast-error variance) between stablecoin supply and crypto prices
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: no evidence that stablecoins push other crypto prices up; issuance reacts to price changes)
entries.notes: Direction of causality opposite to the 'Tether pumps BTC' reading of E26 (outside 2017).

entries.title: The impact of Tether grants on Bitcoin
entries.authors: Wang Chun Wei
entries.mechanism: VAR of Tether issuance on subsequent BTC returns and volume
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: Tether issuance does not affect subsequent BTC returns but does affect volume; Tether trading rises after BTC return declines)

entries.title: The instability of stablecoins
entries.authors: Kun Duan; Andrew Urquhart
entries.mechanism: fractional integration of stablecoin deviations from USD 1; speed of peg correction
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: strong evidence of instability; deviations corrected at different speeds except DAI, which does not converge; BUSD fastest)
entries.notes: Relevant to USDT-margined carry: stablecoin depeg is an unpriced risk (gap A3 in research_gaps). USDT/USDC spot prices are collectable forward.

entries.title: Blockchain Analysis of the Bitcoin Market
entries.authors: Igor Makarov; Antoinette Schoar
entries.mechanism: entity-labelled Bitcoin transaction network: exchanges, miners, large holders
entries.universe: all Bitcoin addresses linked to entities
entries.effect_size: 90% of on-chain transaction volume is not economically meaningful; since 2015 about 75% of real volume is linked to exchanges or exchange-like entities; illegal activity, scams and gambling below 3% of volume
entries.notes: Warning for raw on-chain flow signals: most volume is noise/internal; exchange flows dominate and are cross-exchange arbitrage-driven.

entries.title: The Moby Dick effect: Contagious Bitcoin whales in the crypto market
entries.authors: Nicolás Magner; Aliro Sanhueza
entries.mechanism: Whale Alert wallet<->exchange BTC transfers as a contagion signal for other coins
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: significant contagion mainly 6 and 24 hours after the transfer)

entries.title: The Intraday Bitcoin Response to Tether Minting and Burning Events: Asymmetry, Investor Sentiment, And "Whale Alerts" On Twitter
entries.authors: Aman Saggu
entries.venue: arXiv:2501.05232 (RePEc arx papers; journal version not verified)
entries.mechanism: BTC response to USDT mint/burn events; amplification by public Whale Alert announcements
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: positive BTC response to mints over 5-30 minute windows, fading after 60 minutes; stronger with positive sentiment and Whale Alert announcement; asymmetric vs burns)
entries.notes: Minute-scale positive response vs Wei's (X047) no effect on subsequent (daily) returns: horizon matters.

entries.title: Quantifying Blockchain Extractable Value: How dark is the forest?
entries.authors: Kaihua Qin; Liyi Zhou; Arthur Gervais
entries.mechanism: extractable value from sandwich attacks, liquidations and DEX arbitrage
entries.effect_size: BEV profit USD 540.54M over 32 months across 11,289 addresses; largest single instance USD 4.1M
entries.notes: On-chain arbitrage/liquidation value accrues to specialised searchers; capacity concentrated.

entries.title: Forecasting Bitcoin volatility spikes from whale transactions and CryptoQuant data using Synthesizer Transformer models
entries.authors: Dorien Herremans; Kah Wee Low
entries.mechanism: whale-alert tweets and on-chain/exchange data as predictors of next-day volatility spikes
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN (abstract: model beats state-of-the-art on extreme spikes; backtest reduces drawdown)
entries.notes: Weak source (ML, no effect sizes in abstract).

entries.title: Pricing Cryptocurrency Options
entries.authors: Ai Jun Hou; Weining Wang; Cathy Y H Chen; Wolfgang Karl Härdle
entries.mechanism: stochastic volatility with correlated jumps (SVCJ) vs cojump model for BTC option pricing
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: a sizeable share of price jumps is significantly and contemporaneously anticorrelated with volatility jumps)
entries.notes: Pricing model, not a premium estimate.

entries.title: Forecasting bitcoin volatility: Evidence from the options market
entries.authors: Lai T. Hoang; Dirk G. Baur
entries.mechanism: Deribit implied volatility vs ARMA/HAR forecasts of realised volatility
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN loss values (abstract: IV worse than ARMA/HAR 1 day ahead, better 7, 10 and 15 days ahead; combination best at all horizons)
entries.notes: IV contains information beyond HAR at 1-2 week horizons; DVOL-type data outside gates.

entries.title: Delta hedging bitcoin options with a smile
entries.authors: Carol Alexander; Arben Imeraj
entries.mechanism: smile-adjusted vs Black-Scholes deltas; perpetual vs calendar futures as hedge instrument
entries.market: Deribit BTC options, hourly; BTC perpetual and futures
entries.effect_size: smile-implied deltas cut hedging error variance by over 30% for OTM puts and about 15% on average for short-term OTM calls when the IV curve slopes up; perp basis risk much smaller than calendar futures
entries.notes: Authors' Bitcoin VIX/VRP paper (JAI 2021) remains unverified (SSRN 403); this verified paper gives hedging, not VRP size.

entries.title: Effects of Social Media-Based Peer Opinions on the Prices of Cryptocurrency Options
entries.authors: Da-Hea Kim
entries.mechanism: text-based social-media opinion vs option-implied smile slope and risk-neutral skewness
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: bearish opinion steepens the smile and makes RN skewness more negative; robust to controls; no later reversal)
entries.notes: Skew responds to sentiment; this is about option prices, not underlying returns.

entries.title: Arbitrage in the market for cryptocurrencies
entries.authors: Tommy Crépellière; Matthias Pelster; Stefan Zeisberger
entries.mechanism: cross-exchange arbitrage opportunities over time; informed trading and efficiency
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: opportunities exist but shrank greatly from April 2018; tested strategies can barely exploit them since)
entries.notes: Contradicts the exploitability reading of E30's large gaps for the post-2018 period; consistent with RESULTS_arb_v1 (0 opportunities).

entries.title: Bitcoin arbitrage and exchange default risk
entries.authors: Weiwei Guo; Silvia Intini; Hossein Jahanshahloo
entries.mechanism: exchange default risk, liquidity, fees and blockchain congestion as limits to cross-exchange arbitrage
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: gaps last longer when the riskier exchange has the higher price; capital flows from risky to safe venues track gaps; liquidity speeds arbitrage; fees and congestion slow it)
entries.notes: Post-2022 data included (to 2024). Default-risk pricing means some gaps are compensation, not free money (cf. FTX).

entries.title: Kimchi premium and speculative trading in bitcoin
entries.authors: Yunsung Eom
entries.mechanism: kimchi premium explained by elevated volume and volatility (speculative bubble / belief dispersion)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: volume and volatility explain the premium; relation clearer as bubble grows)
entries.notes: Speculation story vs E33's risk story.

entries.title: Is the Kimchi premium a speculative bubble?
entries.authors: Hyunmin Ok; Jinyong Kim; Yongsik Kim
entries.mechanism: time-varying coefficient re-test of Eom (2021)
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: positive premium-volume/volatility relation not robust over time)
entries.notes: Direct failed robustness of a published kimchi explanation.

entries.title: Nonlinear dynamics of Kimchi premium
entries.authors: Myung Hwan Seo; Bonsoo Koo; Yangzhuoran Fin Yang
entries.mechanism: multi-regime threshold regression: arbitrage only beyond a band; fees set the band
entries.effect_size: long-run steady-state premium 1.24% for BTC; mean reversion only outside threshold band, random walk inside; trading fee positively correlated with the threshold
entries.costs_included: fees as determinant of no-arbitrage band
entries.notes: Previously an unverified lead in LITERATURE_MAP (Seo, Koo & Yang 2024, 1.24%) - now verified via IDEAS. Band structure = friction view.

entries.title: Cryptomarket discounts
entries.authors: Nicola Borri; Kirill Shakhnov
entries.venue: Journal of International Money and Finance 139, 102963
entries.mechanism: relative BTC price discounts across exchange-currency pairs; capital controls, mining location, attention
entries.effect_size: discount half-life 1 day; distribution leptokurtic, right-skewed, standard deviation 3.9%; variability larger under tighter capital controls
entries.effect_unit_horizon: relative price discount; half-life in days
entries.notes: Same authors as E33; half-life gives a mean-reversion speed benchmark.

entries.title: Who are the arbitrageurs? Empirical evidence from Bitcoin traders in the Mt. Gox exchange platform
entries.authors: Pietro Saggese; Alessandro Belmonte; Nicola Dimitri; Angelo Facchini; Rainer Böhme
entries.mechanism: triangular arbitrage profitability by trader expertise
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: one expertise group is on average unprofitable after transaction costs while multi-market skilled traders earn a positive significant premium; skill = fast reaction and order splitting)
entries.notes: Abstract wording on which group is unprofitable is ambiguous; summary kept to 'arbitrage profits concentrated in a few sophisticated users'.

entries.title: Cryptocurrency factor momentum
entries.authors: Christian Fieberg; Gerrit Liedtke; Daniel Metko; Adam Zaremba
entries.mechanism: momentum in anomaly (factor) returns; replication of 34 crypto anomalies
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: past winning factors beat losers, robust across subperiods, comparable to stocks; driven by size and volatility anomalies; originates from price momentum)
entries.notes: Replication-scale study; size/volatility anomalies live in small coins (cf. E22).

entries.title: The Cryptocurrency Trend Factor Revisited: Predictive Information, Portfolio Construction, and Pricing Claims
entries.authors: Yifei Wang; Zhenling Pang
entries.mechanism: code audit and correction of the published crypto trend factor (CTREND): look-ahead, indicators, forecast coverage, accounting
entries.universe: full CTREND universe; largest 100 coins subset
entries.effect_size: after full correction: mean weekly gross return 4.07% -> 0.05%, annualised Sharpe 2.08 -> 0.01, weekly alpha 2.77% -> -1.38% (insignificant); net weekly long-short return at lowest costs 2.93% -> -0.87%; largest-100 gross 2.93% -> 1.00%
entries.costs_included: yes (lowest assumed trading costs for net figures)
entries.oos_or_replication: replication with code audit; published claims fail after correction
entries.notes: Strongest new replication evidence: a published crypto factor collapses after look-ahead and accounting fixes. Posted 2026-11-01, not yet reviewed.

entries.title: On survivor cryptocurrency momentum
entries.authors: Klaus Grobys; Davide Sandretto; Janne Äijö
entries.mechanism: currency-style momentum among survivor coins vs plain top-30 momentum; trimming sensitivity
entries.universe: 9 survivor coins; largest 30 coins per year
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: no momentum among survivors; plain momentum profitable only after trimming; highly sample-dependent even then)
entries.notes: Same first author as E11.

entries.title: Technical trading and cryptocurrencies
entries.authors: Robert Hudson; Andrew Urquhart
entries.mechanism: about 15,000 technical rules with multiple-hypothesis (data-snooping) control
entries.market: two BTC markets and three other cryptocurrencies
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: significant predictability after data-snooping control; breakeven costs above typical costs; but no predictability for Bitcoin out-of-sample, some remains for other coins)
entries.notes: In-sample data-snooping-robust result that fails OOS for BTC - the most liquid asset.

entries.title: Are simple technical trading rules profitable in bitcoin markets?
entries.authors: Niek Deprez; Michael Frömmel
entries.mechanism: 75,360 simple rules (6 classes, daily and intraday), selection after costs with multiple-hypothesis procedure, OOS portfolios
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: selected rule portfolios can beat buy-and-hold out-of-sample, especially risk-adjusted)
entries.notes: Contradicts Hudson & Urquhart's BTC OOS null; claim is mainly risk-adjusted (drawdown) not raw return. Sample period UNKNOWN.

entries.title: Machine learning and the cross-section of cryptocurrency returns
entries.authors: Nusret Cakici; Syed Jawad Hussain Shahzad; Barbara Będowska-Sójka; Adam Zaremba
entries.mechanism: ML models on crypto characteristics; predictability from price, past alpha, illiquidity, momentum
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: most ML strategies profitable after trading costs, but alphas concentrated in hard-to-trade small, illiquid, volatile coins; from the long leg)
entries.notes: Net-of-cost claim conditional on trading illiquid coins - outside the lab's liquid perp universe.

entries.title: Cross-sectional interactions in cryptocurrency returns
entries.authors: Aleksander Mercik; Barbara Będowska-Sójka; Sitara Karim; Adam Zaremba
entries.mechanism: double sorts on 40 characteristics; liquidity x risk x past return interactions
entries.effect_size: OOS long-short of top/bottom interactions: Sharpe ratio above 1; low liquidity raises costs and sustains anomalies
entries.costs_included: UNKNOWN (costs discussed as cause of persistence)
entries.notes: Sample reaches 2023. Multiple-testing scale (40 chars, many pairs) acknowledged only via OOS selection.

entries.title: Psychological anchoring effect and cross section of cryptocurrency returns
entries.authors: Yuecheng Jia; Betty Simkins; Shu Yan; Hongyu Zhang; Jiangyu Zhao
entries.mechanism: nearness to 52-week high (anchoring) predicts cross-sectional returns
entries.effect_size: value-weighted high-minus-low Nearness52 portfolio about 130 bp per week
entries.costs_included: UNKNOWN (abstract says frictions ruled out as explanation)
entries.notes: Copybot tag anchoring_to_high exists; size is gross. Note the CTREND correction (X066) as a warning for weekly crypto factor claims.

entries.title: Crypto trading and Bitcoin prices: evidence from a new database of retail adoption
entries.authors: Raphael Auer; Giulio Cornelli; Sebastian Doerr; Jon Frost; Leonardo Gambacorta
entries.mechanism: price-driven retail entry (trend-chasing adoption) using daily crypto-app usage in 95 countries
entries.effect_size: rising BTC price followed by new-user entry; about 40% of new users are men under 35; about three-quarters of users estimated to have lost money on BTC
entries.oos_or_replication: two exogenous shocks (China mining ban 2021, Kazakhstan 2022) + PVAR
entries.notes: Independent evidence for the trend-chasing retail demand that E04/X001 use to explain carry.

entries.title: Crypto shocks and retail losses
entries.authors: Giulio Cornelli; Sebastian Doerr; Jon Frost; Leonardo Gambacorta
entries.mechanism: flows by investor size around Terra/Luna and FTX
entries.effect_size: UNKNOWN size (abstract: large investors sold while small retail bought; majority of app users lost money on BTC)

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence in Equity and Crypto Markets: Progress, Profitability Evidence, and the Limits of Automated Investing
entries.authors: Linsen Zhu; Mengqing Cai
entries.mechanism: critical review: alpha-translation chain from point-in-time signal to net returns; failure modes (contamination, selection, survivorship, costs, capacity)
entries.market: equities, ETFs, crypto spot, perps, on-chain
entries.effect_size: qualitative: no AI architecture shown to deliver persistent, cross-regime, capacity-aware net alpha in the public record
entries.notes: Review; useful as a checklist of replication failure modes.
